maps.title: Digital infrastructure
maps.question: Which existing system can people use, and who supports it?
maps.intro: Start with findable shared records and practical connectivity. The inventory records useful assets and leads; it is not a live survey.

nodes.title: Findable shared records
nodes.summary: A retained source collection and search index already provide a starting point.
known: Website, governance and ecological records have retained source homes.
Dated captures and original sources are distinct.
checks: Can another permitted contributor find, read and correct one useful record?

links.label: Find the review and upkeep route

nodes.title: Site connectivity
nodes.summary: Existing connectivity is reported; practical coverage needs a current test.
known: An on-site network knowledge contact and remote installer contact are recorded.
The activity-space connection needs a dated outcome.
checks: Trace and test the actual room-to-internet journey.
Confirm fixed-line order, provider and delivery evidence.

nodes.title: Monitoring inventory
nodes.summary: A dated Home Assistant inspection identifies configured devices and apps.
known: Energy and water monitoring configuration was inspected on 7 October.
Stored archives and a history source were located.
checks: Verify one actual reading, timestamp, history/export path and useful operator question.
Configured devices and running apps do not prove present field data.

nodes.title: Services and recovery
nodes.summary: Media, community tools and hosted knowledge have separate operating histories.
known: Different services have separate owners, access and recovery needs.
Historical checks are useful evidence of earlier states.
checks: Name support and recovery ownership per service.
Separate current availability, backup existence and tested restore.

nodes.title: Access request route
nodes.summary: Use service ownership and approved access to turn records into usable resources.
known: Nuno is reported as TDF Bitwarden owner.
Vault ownership does not establish all service permissions.
checks: Confirm the request and approval route, permitted scope and backup contact.
Keep credentials outside the map.

nodes.title: Accountable operation
nodes.summary: Knowledge contacts help diagnose; operating responsibility needs its own evidence.
known: Network knowledge and Closer contribution contacts are recorded.
checks: Who accepts the service outcome, handles failures and maintains the record?
Which changes can that role authorize?

nodes.title: One useful proof
nodes.summary: Retrieve one permitted record or verify one real operating journey with its user.
known: Existing resources allow bounded improvement before a larger platform decision.
checks: Choose a real user, useful result, reviewer and maintenance route.
Record the dated outcome and what still depends on access.

links.label: Evidence for a bounded land result

edges.label: A repair needs an accepted support route
Verify a real reading before extending
Each service needs its own owner

notes: Can use now: retained records and existing role/source routes within permission.
Conditional: shared service availability, recovery, new hosting and compute readiness.
No IP addresses, credentials, internal endpoints or wiring claims are provided.

maps.title: People, roles and access
maps.kicker: Follow a useful piece of work
maps.question: Who contributes, who is accountable, and who can authorize the next step?
maps.intro: Roles may have several people, and people may hold several roles. Contacts, holders, decision authority and current availability need separate evidence.

nodes.title: Hosting and bookings
nodes.summary: Published and reported work links offer a practical entry into arrival and booking questions.
known: Sonja is publicly listed as Space Host.
Bige's hosting, booking and volunteer coordination work is reported.
checks: Confirm current roster and who follows a booking issue through resolution.

nodes.title: Digital knowledge and contribution
nodes.summary: Technical knowledge is useful without implying ownership of every system.
known: Nuno is an on-site network knowledge contact.
Mathijs is a remote installer contact; Paul contributes to Closer.
checks: Confirm current availability and precise contribution scope.
Do not assign Paul to hosting or equate installation with service ownership.

nodes.title: Land knowledge and continuity
nodes.summary: Recent practice, expert advice and practical continuity are different contributions.
known: Bara's recent practice is a handover source.
Ofer's expert knowledge and Dylan's practical continuity are recorded.
checks: Confirm current remit, availability and review/correction route.
Keep the listed Land Lead distinct from other land contributors.

nodes.title: Booking-to-service bridge
nodes.summary: A front-line problem needs a clear route to someone who can act and return an answer.
known: The booking workflow and Closer contribution are known starting points.
checks: Who receives, authorizes, fixes and closes one real issue?
Retrieve service/role information with permitted access.

nodes.title: Delegated decisions
nodes.summary: Public director roles help locate the conversation; actual limits require a decision record.
known: Tonya is listed as Operations Director.
Sam and Luna are listed as co-directors.
checks: Clarify which role can approve which change, spending or contract.
Separate coordination, budget control and signature authority.

nodes.title: Capture, review and upkeep
nodes.summary: Keeping knowledge useful involves distinct work beyond initial documentation.
known: Mapping and professional source homes already exist.
A source record can be captured without being accepted for publication.
checks: Who corrects a source, approves wider sharing and keeps it current?
Test a simple handover to a permitted second reader.

nodes.title: Future offer ownership
nodes.summary: Choose a concrete offer before appointing its operator or assuming a business relationship.
known: AI, learning and income work remains exploratory.
checks: Name the user, operator, payer, support duties and agreement for one pilot.
Distinguish knowledge input from operational commitment.

notes: Can use now: published roles and recorded professional knowledge routes.
Confirm before relying on them: availability, complete mandate, access and delegated authority.
The domain map keeps all 41 role rows; this page follows selected practical journeys.

maps.title: AI and tech revenue
maps.kicker: Useful work before a larger offer
maps.question: What could someone use or pay for, and what would it take to deliver reliably?
maps.intro: Reliable coworking and a useful small result can start with existing resources. Future compute, support and learning offers need user evidence, an operator and workable terms.

nodes.title: Reliable coworking
nodes.summary: Practical working conditions are an immediate route to usefulness.
known: Connectivity and work conditions are recorded priorities.
A limited coworking account provides questions to test.
checks: Observe calls, connectivity, noise and comfort with a real user.
Identify the most costly friction and verify the improvement.

nodes.title: First useful result
nodes.summary: The first aim is a result a real person at TDF can use.
known: Practical usefulness is distinct from payment.
Existing knowledge and systems can support bounded work.
checks: Select the exact task, beneficiary, reviewer and done condition.

nodes.title: November experiment
nodes.summary: A small gathering could bring new people; format and delivery remain open.
known: Learning, nature and human flourishing are recorded themes.
The gathering need not require payment or a hackathon format.
checks: Choose the audience, format, host and delivery capacity.
Confirm dates and a useful reason to attend before announcing.

nodes.title: Future compute or hosting
nodes.summary: Local AI and hosting are possibilities requiring evidence of capacity and reliability.
known: Local compute, storage and paid support have been discussed.
checks: Compare existing, rented and local capacity for the actual use.
Verify support, permitted access, recovery and full costs before a service promise.

nodes.title: Operator and agreement
nodes.summary: TDF-operated, independent and partner-operated offers have different obligations.
known: Several possible operator models are recorded.
checks: Agree who owns hardware, receives payments, pays costs and handles departure.
Confirm entity, access, support and signing authority.

nodes.title: Demand, income and costs
nodes.summary: Actual use and payments need evidence; equipment finance is a separate input.
known: Meaningful income is a recorded aim, not a completed result.
checks: Test a useful offer with a real user and payer.
Separate revenue, operating costs, capital and recurring support workload.

nodes.title: One bounded pilot
nodes.summary: Choose the smallest useful version with a reviewer and upkeep route.
known: One practical result can inform later learning and commercial decisions.
checks: Record uptake, user feedback, delivery effort and any attributable payment.
Use the result to choose continue, change or stop.

links.label: Capital and outside funding are separate

notes: Can test now: cowork improvements, retrieval and a small learning/practical experiment within permission.
Conditional: new compute capacity, paid support and larger offsites or events.
November gathering, attributable income, a substantial 2027 event and enduring identity remain separate aims.
No price, revenue forecast, equipment order or visitor commitment is assumed.

maps.title: Regenerative finance and outside funding
maps.kicker: Connect an outcome to a suitable route
maps.question: Which bounded ecological result could receive support, through which entity and with what obligations?
maps.intro: Existing public backing mechanisms and researched leads provide routes to investigate. Money received, eligible applicants and current project commitments need their own evidence.

nodes.title: Published TDF backing routes
nodes.summary: Public material presents several ways to support TDF.
known: Token backing, private lending, prepaid stays and monthly support are published mechanisms.
checks: Verify current terms and actual received, restricted or owed amounts.
Separate backing mechanisms from free operating cash.

nodes.title: OASA funding models
nodes.summary: Village-fund and catalytic-capital material describe different support models.
known: Published models include donation and repayable instruments.
checks: Confirm actual TDF access, allocation and conditions.
Do not infer a transaction from the model.

nodes.title: One bounded land result
nodes.summary: Existing water, soil and stewardship knowledge can inform a useful project.
known: Land records and practical handover sources are retained.
checks: Name the place, useful outcome, scope, owner and maintenance path.
Distinguish current practice, planned work and rejected proposal bundles.

nodes.title: Funding and obligations ledger
nodes.summary: The current financial picture needs receipts, restrictions, future duties and decision records.
known: Published routes and dated proposal records provide starting evidence.
checks: Recover existing applications, decisions, receipts and liabilities.
Keep loans, prepaid services, donations and earned income distinct.

nodes.title: Baseline, outcome and source rights
nodes.summary: Reliable evidence supports a land result but does not create impact by itself.
known: Ecological records and a dated monitoring inventory are retained.
checks: Establish method, current readings, baseline, uncertainty and correction route.
Confirm permission and attribution before sharing source material.

nodes.title: Applicant and delivery capacity
nodes.summary: The recipient, signatory and delivery team must fit the actual project.
known: TDF, OASA and the operating entity have distinct roles in retained material.
checks: Identify legal recipient, mandate, signatory, costs and co-funding.
Check who can deliver and maintain the result after support ends.

nodes.title: Reasoned funding fit
nodes.summary: Match one useful project to a plausible route after recovering existing work.
known: Community support, grants, learning programmes and investment are different instruments.
Dated outside-funding leads already have a research owner.
checks: Recheck the current official call and full conditions before application work.
Record pursue, later or not fit with reasons and a responsible next step.

links.label: Earned customer income has its own test

edges.label: A useful result needs credible evidence

notes: Can use now: retained land sources and dated published-mechanism research.
Conditional: current call fit, eligible applicant, allocation, delivery and upkeep.
No funding is described as secured and no deadline is reproduced without a fresh check.
Monitoring, modelled scenarios and marketing plans are not verified ecological outcomes or credits.
